items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Papa French thought he would send John... I walked in there... he says, 'But I’ll tell you what... I’m going to make you my band leader.'

ctx.x: Yeah. It was very nice to see him. I told him all about that. He was like, me? I said yeah, you. But in 1976 Albert Papa French, who took over the band from Papa Celestin, which was like the oldest established band in the world, continuing like from 1910, he called my dad to make a job. And my dad said, “Albert, I’m sick, but I’ll send my son.” So he was like, “Okay man.” Well Papa French thought he would send John, my older brother you know. And I walked in there, at that time I had my big Jimi Hendrix tall…

says, “Who are you man?” I says, “I’m Picket’s son man.” And he says, “Oh wait, we thought he was going to send John, man.” Well my whole ego just took a nosedive. He said, “But I’ll tell you what, you know some songs?” I said, “Yeah I know a few songs, I’ve been practicing a little bit.” So he says, “Well look I’m going to make you my band leader. Whatever you call tonight, that’s what we’re going to play.” And then, what a relief that was. And I learned a lot that night, just about being a band leader. Because…
